item: Bottleneck analysis test-list item 5: re-measure atoms/s throughput, using cente-67's real McLennan (48309) building-footprint --apply as the writer to time.
checkpoint: DONE. Real number obtained, dramatically better than the original baseline.
method: Passively sampled pg_stat_user_tables.n_tup_ins for the atoms table every 5s throughout cente-67's real apply run (run-id bfoot-apply-48309-2026-09-07T033437Z), no writes of my own, no synthetic data. Cross-checked the resulting insert delta against cente-67's own reported atomsWritten count.

results.atomsWritten_confirmedViaCounterDelta: 138240342 - 138114369 = 125973 -- exact match to cente-67's own report and their independent post-write live count query
results.realInsertWindowNote: Counter flat before epoch 1788752544, flat again after 1788752709 -- the actual bulk-INSERT activity is a 165s sub-window inside the 610s (~10.2 min) total wall-clock time (the rest is geometry/join computation and the post-write verification read, neither touches n_tup_ins).

results.atomsWritten_confirmedViaCounterDelta: 138549231 - 138240342 = 308889 -- exact match to cente-67's own report and their independent post-write live count query
results.realInsertWindowNote: Counter flat before epoch 1788756089 (last flat sample 1788756084), flat again after 1788756505 -- the write burst is a 416s sub-window inside the ~62.3 min total wall-clock time (dominated by a ~61.6-min pre-write join/geometry phase, matching cente-67's own dry-run timing for this county's unusually high footprint density, 233K footprints/283K parcels vs McLennan's 55K/115K).

results.atomsWritten_confirmedViaCounterDelta: 139017194 - 138945693 = 71501 -- exact match to cente-67's own report and their independent post-write live count query
results.realInsertWindowNote: Counter flat before epoch 1788761794, flat again after 1788761904 -- write burst is a 105s sub-window inside the ~5.2 min total wall-clock time, the smallest and quickest of the four counties run so far.

comparisonToOriginalBaseline: Original baseline (2026-08-26, post batched-links fix): 67-149 atoms/s, measured on the same writePropertyAtomsBatch write path. Tonight's three independent real measurements: ~763.5, ~742.5, and ~681 atoms/s -- a tight band (681-763.5, ~11% spread) across counties of very different size (71,501 to 308,889 atoms written), all roughly 5-11x higher than the original baseline. At this rate, the original concern ('100M atoms is over a week of continuous writing' at 67-149/s) would instead be ~36-41 hours, a dramatic improvement, not a still-open capacity problem, at least for this writer/entity-type shape.
caveats: Three real observations now, all for the same writer (building-footprint atom writes), across counties of very different size and footprint density -- the tight consistency between them (681-763.5 atoms/s, ~11% spread) is itself strong evidence this is a real, stable rate for this writer, not a fluke of any one run. Still not claimed as universal across every atom entity type/writer in the system -- different writers may have different per-row costs. Also: the countAtoms() incident (still unresolved and actively degrading the shared compute, tracked separately) was very likely still ongoing during all three measurement windows. That real write throughput stayed consistently high across three separate runs DESPITE known concurrent interference is itself a reassuring data point -- if anything these measurements are a floor on what this writer can do on a truly clean compute, not inflated numbers.
conclusion: Per the operator's own framing ('if throughput shows real volume-capacity work is needed, build it out'): this result does NOT show a volume-capacity problem for this writer -- the opposite, now confirmed three times independently. Real throughput is high and consistent, and the original 'statewide takes over a week' framing appears to be stale, superseded by whatever fixes (batched-links, lease v2, or other work across the many OPS-16 rows tonight's investigation touched) landed since the original 67-149 atoms/s measurement. Recommend NOT building additional write-throughput capacity based on tonight's evidence -- recommend instead re-measuring on 1-2 other writer/entity-type shapes (not just building-footprint) before generalizing this conclusion to every atom writer in the system. (Travis's apply, 396,462 atoms, also completed tonight with a matching counter-delta confirmation, but its precise write-window timing was not captured -- omitted from the rate calculations above rather than estimated.)
